title: Why Conservatives Should Root for Taylor Swift
gist: Joshua Sohn argues pro-family conservatives should cheer Taylor Swift's marriage-and-kids era: celebrity fertility is associated with fans' fertility (per an IFS 2026 birth-projection report), and liberal audiences are receptive to pro-marriage messaging from the right messenger, as the reception of her song 'Babylon' shows.

insights.claim: The IFS 2026 report on American birth projections states that celebrity fertility is associated with the fertility of fans, and suggests the demographic effect of Taylor Swift having kids could exceed that of nationwide child tax credits.
insights.speaker: Joshua L. Sohn
insights.so_what: A claimed cultural channel for fertility that may rival fiscal policy; watch celebrity family-formation as a soft demographic driver.
insights.quote: celebrity fertility really is associated with the fertility of fans
insights.locator: A Swift Rebound on Family Issues?

insights.claim: If Swift has children and writes maternal ballads, it could counteract the common cultural message that motherhood is a brutal game not worth playing, with better odds than anything else on the cultural horizon.
insights.speaker: Joshua L. Sohn
insights.so_what: Speculative cultural-narrative shift on motherhood; low-confidence signal for family-formation attitudes among young women.

insights.claim: Swift's rumored move into Hollywood screenwriting could help Hollywood break from its long-standing aversion to romance, which the author links to Americans' retreat from sex and dating.
insights.speaker: Joshua L. Sohn
insights.so_what: Hypothesis that media content drives dating behavior; a romance revival in film/TV would be a content-demand tell.
insights.locator: First, consider romance and a revival of dating for marriage.

insights.claim: Contrary to the culture-war stereotype, liberal Americans are receptive to messages of monogamy, marriage, children, community and even religion, so long as they come from the right messenger.
insights.speaker: Joshua L. Sohn
insights.so_what: Pro-family messaging need not be partisan; cultural nudges via cross-partisan celebrities may move attitudes among groups with falling marriage rates.
insights.quote: contrary to the culture-war stereotype, liberal Americans are receptive to messages of monogamy, marriage, children, community, even religion

insights.claim: Marriage and childbearing rates are declining among liberals in particular, and Democrats are increasingly disinclined to marry and have kids.
insights.speaker: Joshua L. Sohn
insights.so_what: Partisan divergence in family formation feeds into long-run electoral demographics and fertility differentials.

insights.claim: Swift's song 'Babylon', released September 25, 2026, praises community and religion and implicitly favors monogamy over hookup culture, and was well received by mainstream outlets such as The Cut and Elle.
insights.speaker: Joshua L. Sohn
insights.so_what: Mainstream approval of a pro-settling-down narrative is a small data point on shifting cultural attitudes toward commitment.

insights.claim: Swift has moved from presumed-conservative country ingenue to mid-2010s liberal 'girlboss' icon to a centrist or big-tent figure, giving her unusually broad dominance across the cultural spectrum.
insights.speaker: Joshua L. Sohn
insights.so_what: Her broad reach makes her a rare cross-audience cultural distribution channel.
insights.quote: she’s never been more dominant across the cultural spectrum

insights.claim: The author argues Swift's visible marriage (e.g. pointing to her ring and shouting 'that's my husband!' after Travis Kelce scored) is strong public relations for the institution of marriage.
insights.speaker: Joshua L. Sohn
insights.so_what: Illustrates the soft-power marketing of marriage; qualitative, not measured.
insights.quote: It’s hard to imagine better PR for the institution of marriage.
